channel.title: GainUtility Blog
channel.description: Practical, problem-first guides from GainUtility — a collection of fast browser-based tools for PDF, image, JSON, developer, and SEO work.

item.title: How to Remove a Background From an Image
item.description: A plain background is the easy case: sample the colour, remove it, check the edges, and download a transparent PNG. All in your browser.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Make a Transparent PNG
item.description: A transparent background lets an image sit on any page colour without a box around it. Here's how to produce one in your browser.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Compress Images Without Losing Too Much Quality
item.description: Image size has two dials — dimensions and quality. Change them in the right order and the picture still looks good.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Resize an Image to an Exact Pixel Size
item.description: Upload forms ask for exact pixel sizes and KB limits. Here's how to hit the numbers without opening a photo editor.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Prepare Product Photos for Your Online Store
item.description: Consistent, clean product photos come from plain backdrops and careful edges. Here's the workflow for a catalog that looks intentional.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Merge Multiple PDFs Into One File
item.description: Combining PDFs is mostly about order and naming. Do both deliberately and one merged file is easier to share, submit, and find later.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Split a PDF and Keep Only the Pages You Need
item.description: Most splits are range extraction, not division in half. Pick the pages, keep only those, and cut a 20-page scan down to the two you wanted.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Convert PDF Pages to JPG
item.description: When a PDF needs to be an image, each page becomes one JPG. Pick the pages and the resolution, then export them as images.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Convert JPG Images to a PDF
item.description: Turn a set of images into one PDF in reading order, so everything lands in a single file you can submit, email, or keep together.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Compress a PDF Without Losing What You Need
item.description: A smaller PDF is only useful if it stays readable. See where the size comes from, then compress in steps you can check.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Add a Watermark to a PDF
item.description: A watermark marks a document as draft, owned, or shared — without getting in the way of the content. Here's how to place one sensibly.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Fix a PDF That's Too Big to Upload
item.description: When a form rejects a PDF for size, work backwards: check the limit, find the heavy pages, then shrink in steps until it fits.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: What Box-Shadow Values Real Websites Actually Use
item.description: We downloaded the homepages of the top 1,000 sites and counted every box-shadow in their CSS: 33,438 declarations across 533 reachable sites. Measured offsets, blur, spread, color, and layering — with the dataset to download.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: box-shadow vs filter: drop-shadow() — Which CSS Shadow to Use
item.description: box-shadow draws the element's border box; filter: drop-shadow() follows the alpha shape of an image. Same-looking values are not interchangeable — the blur number even means something different.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: Soft Shadow CSS Recipes That Don't Turn Out Muddy
item.description: Copy-ready soft box-shadow values for cards, floating panels, and hover states — plus why stacked shadows go muddy, and the alpha-first method that keeps them clean.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: Neumorphism Box Shadow: The Two-Layer Formula and Its Limits
item.description: How soft-UI neumorphism works: one light layer, one dark layer, background matched to surface. Copy the formula, the inset variant, and where the style still makes sense.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Read and Fix Unreadable JSON From an API
item.description: Minified API responses are one long line until you adopt the three-habit routine: format first, validate second, diff after a change.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Make a QR Code That Actually Scans
item.description: The URL and the error-correction level decide whether a QR code scans the first time. Get those right and the rest is easy.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Tune CSS Gradients, Shadows, and Contrast Without Guessing
item.description: The last ten percent of a UI is gradients, shadows, and contrast — the fiddly details that eat time until you preview them instead of guessing.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Write a Page Title and Meta Description
item.description: The title and meta description are the ad your page shows in search results. Write them like real sentences people read.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: Why I Started Building Small Browser Tools for Everyday Problems
item.description: A short, honest note on why the site exists: not to be a giant platform, but to remove small daily friction with focused browser utilities.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Convert a PDF to Word Without Losing the Text
item.description: PDF to Word means pulling text out of a fixed-layout file and putting it into a flowing document. What converts cleanly, what has to be rebuilt, and when OCR has to come first.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Convert a Word Document to PDF
item.description: PDF is the format that renders the same on every machine. Convert a .docx by reading its structure, laying it into pages, and checking the three things that move.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: Are Online PDF Tools Safe? How to Check What Happens to Your File
item.description: Some online PDF tools upload your document; others never send it anywhere. How to tell which one you are using, what the major tools' own terms say about deletion, and the checks worth running.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: PDF File Size Limits: How Big Can Your PDF Be?
item.description: There is no single PDF size limit - each destination publishes its own. The documented limits for email, messaging, website uploads and application portals, and how to get under the one you are facing.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Check Your Robots.txt and Sitemap Before You Submit Them
item.description: Two small files decide what a crawler may read and what it should be pointed at. Reading both for a minute catches the mistakes that quietly hide pages.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Preview a Link Before You Share It
item.description: A shared link is read as a title, a line of text and a picture. Render that card first and you catch the broken image and the cut-off headline before anyone else does.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Make a Favicon From Any Image
item.description: A logo that looks sharp at 400px usually turns to mud at 16px. Starting from the right crop and the right sizes is what keeps a tab icon recognisable.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Compare Two JSON Files Without Losing Your Place
item.description: Two JSON documents can differ in one number and still look identical line by line. Comparing by path instead of by eye turns the difference into a short list.
item.author: GainUtility

item.title: How to Protect a PDF With a Password
item.description: A password stops the wrong person opening a file; the printing and copying permissions are a separate setting. Knowing which is which decides whether you set the right one.
item.author: GainUtility
